name: EASY PACKET 1 #01  The Capture Signature
reason: File magic d4 c3 b2 a1 indicates classic little-endian, microsecond-resolution PCAP; capinfos independently reports pcap. This is file-level evidence, not a packet protocol field. The platform may call this libpcap.
platform_validation: Candidate pcap reported rejected by teammate; exact accepted phrase unresolved.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #03  Destination at Layer 2
reason: Ethernet destination address; independently verified from the first six frame bytes.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #04  Source at Layer 2
reason: Ethernet source address; independently verified from frame bytes 6–11.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #07  The 20-Byte Header
reason: IHL is 5, which is 20 bytes. Garcia reports that the accepted flag includes the literal units suffix: 20 bytes.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #08  Total Packet Weight
reason: IPv4 Total Length is 504 bytes; the Ethernet header is not included.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #09  Packet Identity
reason: The IPv4 Identification field is hexadecimal 0xbed2, decimal 48850. The flag candidate uses Wireshark's hexadecimal notation; the grader's numeric representation is unvalidated.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #18  Push and Acknowledge
reason: TCP flags value is 0x018. PSH and ACK are set; SYN, FIN, RST, and URG are clear. The underscore separator is a submission-format candidate, not an observed grader requirement.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #20  Push to the Application
answer: Push buffered data to the receiving application without waiting for more data
reason: PSH requests the push function: make buffered data available to the receiving user/application rather than waiting for additional data to fill a buffer. It is not a record boundary or a guarantee of immediate application scheduling. This conceptual answer is established, but the challenge does not disclose the exact phrase its flag matcher expects. Do not invent an accepted flag spelling. Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.9.1.2

name: EASY PACKET 1 #21  Speak HTTP
reason: The TCP payload starts GET /statuses/replies.xml HTTP/1.1 and is decoded as HTTP.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #29  The Exposed Credentials
reason: Authorization is Basic dXNlcnRlc3Q6cGFzc3dvcmQ=. Base64 decoding yields username usertest and password password, separated by a colon. These are challenge-supplied packet contents.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: EASY PACKET 1 #30  Cleartext on the Wire
answer: HTTP Basic credentials are recoverable over unencrypted HTTP; use HTTPS (HTTP over TLS)
reason: Base64 is encoding, not encryption: an observer can recover the username/password. Protect credential transport with HTTPS/TLS. This is the semantic answer; the exact compound phrase expected inside the flag is not specified. Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7617.html#section-1

name: ACT 1 - FIRST SIGNAL: Domain Membership
reason: Captured DNS realm is FIRSTTOLAST.TECH. Garcia reports that the grader accepts the short/NetBIOS name FIRSTTOLAST instead of the DNS realm.
platform_validation: Accepted per Garcia Day1 report; not independently retested in our account.

name: ACT 1 - FIRST SIGNAL: Calling Home
reason: The compromised host sends repeated short-path POSTs and a FormBook-pattern GET check-in to this IP. Domain www.grinswakebthu.info, path /irpw/, parameter 2kn1, fixed Firefox/39.0 user agent. Prior ACT 4 OSINT analysis independently preserved official ET signature 2050745 and matching network evidence. This is one confirmed C2 answer, not a claim that every contacted external IP is malicious.

name: ACT 2 - THE COMPROMISE: Who Is brolf?
reason: SAMR UserInfo21 pairs brolf with full_name Becka Rolf in one response.

name: ACT 2 - THE COMPROMISE: RAT Check-In
reason: 264 HTTP requests use the NetSupport Manager/1.3 user agent. The request target can be absolute-form http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm; the requested path is /fakeurl.htm. HTTP is carried on TCP port 443 in this capture, which does not make it TLS.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Compromised Endpoint
reason: This source sends a plaintext STRRAT victim-profile beacon to 141.98.10.79:12132.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Endpoint MAC
reason: Ethernet source on the confirmed victim's STRRAT beacon.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Endpoint Name
reason: The host field in the decoded STRRAT beacon is DESKTOP-SKBR25F. Kerberos machine-account desktop-skbr25f$ independently corroborates it in frame 58.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Compromised Account
reason: Kerberos and SAMR identify account ccollier; the STRRAT beacon also carries ccollier.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: User Identity
reason: LDAP frame 9759 has sn=Collier and givenName=Clark; LDAP frame 10317 has displayName=Clark Collier and the matching user DN. SAMR frame 1070 pairs ccollier with Clark Collier, bridging the account to the directory name.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: C2 Destination
reason: Destination of the recurring STRRAT beacons; destination TCP port 12132. Do not confuse this with the benign ip-api.com geolocation lookup.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Malware Family
reason: The application payload literally begins ping|STRRAT| and includes the victim profile and version 1.6. No public solution page is needed for attribution.

name: ACT 3 - MALWARE INVESTIGATION: Beacon Evidence
reason: The fourth pipe-separated beacon field is DESKTOP-SKBR25F. The complete first beacon is saved in act3-first-beacon.txt.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Lumma Victim
reason: The source of both Chrome and Edge victim-fingerprinting requests is 10.1.21.58.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Victim MAC
reason: Ethernet source address on the infected host's C2 request.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Victim Hostname
reason: DHCP Host Name is DESKTOP-ES9F3ML; DHCP offers/acknowledges 10.1.21.58. NBNS independently advertises the same hostname.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Compromised User
reason: Kerberos names gwyatt; the SAMR user-information response confirms the account.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Full User Name
reason: The same SAMR UserInfo21 response pairs account gwyatt with full name Gabriel Wyatt. Preserve the space in the raw answer; the challenge does not specify underscore normalization.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Malicious Domain
reason: DNS maps whitepepper.su to 153.92.1.49; HTTP Host confirms the same domain.

name: ACT 4 - LUMMA IN THE ROOM: Fingerprint API
reason: The API endpoint is /api/set_agent. Query strings supply victim ID, token, agent=Chrome/Edge, and optionally act=log; they are not part of the requested path.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Map the Network
reason: These three client IPv4 addresses are ordered numerically. The gateway is 10.3.14.1. Despite the question describing all three as Windows, .135 exhibits Apple/macOS traffic.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Host One MAC
reason: Ethernet source on an IPv4 packet sent by 10.3.14.131.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Host Two MAC
reason: Ethernet source on packets from 10.3.14.134; DHCP also identifies this host as Knutson-PC.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Host Three MAC

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Find the Victims
reason: The .131 host accesses the Spora payment domain; .134 emits Cerber-pattern UDP/6892 traffic and visits the Cerber payment portal. These are the two infected endpoints in ascending order.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: First Ransomware
reason: The first host accesses spora.biz, the ransomware-specific domain. The HTTP stream includes redirects and DDoS-Guard interstitials; those pages alone are not proof of executable delivery. Family attribution combines this ransomware-specific domain, the challenge's infection context, and primary Spora research.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Second Ransomware
reason: UDP destination port 6892 and p27dokhpz2n7nvgr.1nmrtq.top match independently published Cerber post-infection behavior. The portal paths include a victim identifier, language selection, captcha, and bitcoin resources.

name: ACT 5 - FINAL INCIDENT: Final Assessment
reason: The third client exhibits ordinary Apple services and Reddit browsing, with neither ransomware-specific pattern attributed to .131 and .134. Clean means no observed evidence of infection in this capture, not a forensic guarantee about the endpoint.
